twitter-odeo-podcast-pivot.body: On June 28, 2005, Apple built podcast subscriptions into iTunes; within two days subscriptions passed one million, and Odeo's entire podcasting business went obsolete overnight. The next March, an internal hackathon produced Jack Dorsey's SMS status-update pitch: Twitter.
twitter-odeo-podcast-pivot.coda: Odeo, the company Twitter was built inside, was sold off in 2007.

youtube-tune-in-hook-up.title: The Domain Registered on Valentine's Day
youtube-tune-in-hook-up.body: youtube.com was registered on February 14, 2005, and its founders later told of a dating-site concept modeled on Hot or Not. Jawed Karim denied attending the dinner party the story hinges on, and Steve Chen conceded it reads like a marketing narrative.
youtube-tune-in-hook-up.coda: What Karim cited instead was trouble finding tsunami footage online.

duan-buffett-lunch.title: The Buffett Lunch
duan-buffett-lunch.body: In 2006 a Guangdong electronics manufacturer won the annual charity auction for lunch with Warren Buffett, paying $620,100. He brought along a 26-year-old who had just quit an American company and had no clear plan yet.
duan-buffett-lunch.coda: The manufacturer was Duan Yongping. The young man was Colin Huang, who later founded Pinduoduo.

blackberry-iphone-2007.title: BlackBerry Saw the Flaws
blackberry-iphone-2007.body: In January 2007, BlackBerry co-CEO Jim Balsillie and chairman Mike Lazaridis watched the iPhone unveiling. Lazaridis's list of flaws was accurate: no physical keyboard, weak security, poor battery, glass typing. Every item was real. Balsillie's reply was, "It's OK, we'll be fine."
blackberry-iphone-2007.coda: BlackBerry's market share eroded to the iPhone in the years that followed.

dvorak-iphone-2007.title: Dvorak Says Pull the Plug
dvorak-iphone-2007.body: On March 28, 2007, columnist John C. Dvorak wrote that phone margins were thin and Nokia and Motorola already dominant, so Apple should hand the iPhone design to some "suckers" and walk away. Given Apple's history in that market, the reasoning was not unreasonable.
dvorak-iphone-2007.coda: He later said that once he actually held the phone, he regretted the call.

auctomatic-taggar-yc.title: The One Who Had to Learn to Code
auctomatic-taggar-yc.body: In 2007 two Irish teenage brothers brought a homemade e-commerce tool into Y Combinator and merged their company with one run by two Oxford graduates. Neither of the Oxford pair could program. One of them was told to learn, fast.
auctomatic-taggar-yc.coda: That one was Harj Taggar, later Y Combinator's first non-founder partner.

justintv-backpack-cruise.title: The Livestreaming Backpack
justintv-backpack-cruise.body: In March 2007 a man strapped a webcam to a baseball cap and began livestreaming his life around San Francisco, twenty-four hours a day, wearing a homemade laptop-backpack rig built by a friend who had dropped out of MIT.
justintv-backpack-cruise.coda: The friend who built it was Kyle Vogt, who later founded Cruise, acquired by GM for over $1 billion.

stackoverflow-blog-post.title: The Anti-Experts-Exchange
stackoverflow-blog-post.body: On April 16, 2008, a programmer posted on his own blog that he wanted to build an "anti-Experts-Exchange" question-and-answer site for programmers, without the paywalls and search-engine gaming he found nauseating about the incumbent.
stackoverflow-blog-post.coda: In 2021 the site was sold to Prosus for 1.8 billion dollars.

zune-leap-year-freeze.title: Day 366
zune-leap-year-freeze.body: Near midnight Pacific time on 31 December 2008, every Zune 30 froze solid, nicknamed Z2K9. The cause was an infinite loop in a power-chip driver that could only trigger on a leap year's 366th day. No patch existed; the only fix was letting the battery die.
zune-leap-year-freeze.coda: The remedy shipped by Microsoft was to wait for the device to run out of power.

china-wang-jian-alibaba-cloud.title: The Liar Who Built the Cloud
china-wang-jian-alibaba-cloud.body: Around 2012, with Alibaba Cloud years into heavy investment and no visible product, staff told Jack Ma directly that Wang Jian was a fraud. Close to eighty percent of the engineering team quit. Ma's reply: fund it a billion yuan a year for ten years, then judge it.
china-wang-jian-alibaba-cloud.coda: Ten years later, the fraud's project turned a profit.

taobao-double11-2009.title: 27 merchants
taobao-double11-2009.body: On November 11, 2009, Taobao Mall rounded up twenty-seven brands to fill a slow sales week; the plan had called for over thirty, but merchants kept dropping out. A civil servant named Yan Jun in Shanxi placed the day's first order, 150 yuan of phone credit, at 00:00:03.
taobao-double11-2009.coda: Sales that day reached 52 million yuan, ten times an ordinary day.

cloudflare-hbs-elective.title: An Elective at HBS
cloudflare-hbs-elective.body: In 2009 a programmer took a leave of absence to study for an MBA at Harvard Business School. He had spent years running an anti-spam volunteer project on the side. He mentioned it in class one day. A classmate said it should be a real product.
cloudflare-hbs-elective.coda: That classmate was Michelle Zatlyn, later Cloudflare's co-founder and COO.

china-3q-war.title: Choose One
china-3q-war.body: On November 3, 2010, Tencent forced a pop-up choice: uninstall 360 or QQ would stop running. Ma Huateng warned users might be wiped out within three days. Days later the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology ordered both sides to restore compatibility.
china-3q-war.coda: The regulator ended it, not the market or either company.

china-thousand-groupon-war.title: The Thousand-Groupon War
china-thousand-groupon-war.body: China's first group-buying site launched in 2010; portals and social networks piled in within months. By August 2011, more than 5,000 group-buying companies were competing — the 'Thousand-Groupon War.' By mid-2014, only 176 sites remained standing.
china-thousand-groupon-war.coda: Fewer than two hundred of five thousand survived.

semver-dependency-hell.title: SemVer's Own Exemption
semver-dependency-hell.body: In 2010 GitHub cofounder Tom Preston-Werner published semver.org, proposing MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH to end 'dependency hell.' The spec itself carves out an exception: during the 0.y.z 'initial development' phase, anything may change at any time — a stage most packages never actually leave.
semver-dependency-hell.coda: Most published packages never leave the version range the rule does not bind.

instagram-burbn-cut.title: What Got Cut From Burbn
instagram-burbn-cut.body: Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger spent nearly a year building a full-featured check-in app called Burbn, then judged their own finished iPhone build cluttered. They stripped it down to photos, comments, and likes, and shipped the result eight weeks later as Instagram.
instagram-burbn-cut.coda: Within a week of launch it had 100,000 users.

tz-database-lawsuit.title: The Lawsuit Over the Time Zone Database
tz-database-lawsuit.body: In October 2011 astrology-software maker Astrolabe sued the tz database's maintainers, claiming its zone data infringed an atlas it published. The mailing list and FTP server went dark. ICANN stepped in to host the database; Astrolabe withdrew the suit in February 2012.
tz-database-lawsuit.coda: An astrology company's copyright claim over sunrise tables was withdrawn without payment.

instagram-facebook-2012.title: A Billion for a Filter
instagram-facebook-2012.body: In April 2012 Facebook announced it was paying $1 billion for Instagram, a 13-person team with no revenue. On The Daily Show, Jon Stewart asked, "A billion dollars of money? For a thing that kind of ruins your pictures?" Measured against team size and revenue, the question was not unfair.
instagram-facebook-2012.coda: The deal is now cited routinely as one of the best acquisitions in tech history.

didi-alibaba-resignation.title: From Alibaba to taxis
didi-alibaba-resignation.body: Cheng Wei spent eight years at Alibaba, working up to deputy general manager of Alipay's consumer business. In June 2012 he quit and, with Wu Rui and Li Xiang, started a taxi-hailing app. When it launched on September 9, only sixteen drivers were online at once.
didi-alibaba-resignation.coda: Two months later, more than a hundred drivers were online at the same time.

knight-capital-power-peg.title: The Eighth Server
knight-capital-power-peg.body: Knight Capital pushed new trading code to eight servers; only seven took it. The eighth still ran dead Power Peg code, retired years earlier, which live orders woke up. In 45 minutes Knight built $3.5B long and $3.15B short. The SEC's finding: nobody reviewed the incomplete deploy.
knight-capital-power-peg.coda: Knight was acquired by a rival within a week of the loss.

dnnresearch-week-of-bidding.title: A Week of Bidding
dnnresearch-week-of-bidding.body: In 2012 a University of Toronto professor and his two graduate students crushed the field in an image-recognition contest, then incorporated a shell company to sell themselves. Google, Microsoft, Baidu, and DeepMind spent a week bidding against each other for it.
dnnresearch-week-of-bidding.coda: Hinton chose Google. One of the two students was Ilya Sutskever.

xiaohongshu-name.title: Not that little red book
xiaohongshu-name.body: Most people assume the name points at the other red book. The founder's own account is duller: Bain & Company and the Stanford Graduate School of Business, the firm he worked at and the school he attended, both run on red.
xiaohongshu-name.coda: Translated into English, the name comes out identical to the other one anyway.

china-wechat-red-envelope-pearl-harbor.title: Pearl Harbor, Digital
china-wechat-red-envelope-pearl-harbor.body: Around Chinese New Year 2014, WeChat's red-envelope feature went live; users grabbed over 40 million red packets within days. On the app Laiwang, Jack Ma called it a 'Pearl Harbor sneak attack' — effective short-term, he wrote, but healthy long-term growth mattered more.
china-wechat-red-envelope-pearl-harbor.coda: The red envelope became a payments funnel.

heartbleed-two-person-team.title: A Team of Four
heartbleed-two-person-team.body: Heartbleed's missing bounds check entered OpenSSL's heartbeat extension in December 2011 and sat unnoticed for two years until independent researchers found it in April 2014. At the time, the codebase behind most of the web's HTTPS traffic was maintained by four volunteers, one full-time.
heartbleed-two-person-team.coda: The fix shipped the same day the bug was disclosed.

goto-fail-duplicate.title: The Duplicate Jump
goto-fail-duplicate.body: Inside Apple's SSLVerifySignedServerKeyExchange, a goto fail; line was duplicated. The second copy sat outside any if, so the function always jumped past the signature check and returned success regardless.
goto-fail-duplicate.coda: The duplicate line ran unchanged on the affected systems for months.

ntp-harlan-stenn.title: Who Sets the Clock
ntp-harlan-stenn.body: Banks, exchanges and satellite systems synchronize against NTP. David Mills designed the protocol; the reference implementation is now led, largely alone, by Harlan Stenn. In March 2015 trade press ran the headline 'NTP Needs Money: Is A Foundation The Answer?'
ntp-harlan-stenn.coda: The foundation is still fundraising toward its budget.

alphago-lee-sedol-2016.title: Stone One Hundred and Two
alphago-lee-sedol-2016.body: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol four games to one in Seoul in March 2016; Lee's only win came in game four. Afterward he said he had made a critical error early in game one, calling the computer's play there excellent and one move unlike anything a human player would choose.
alphago-lee-sedol-2016.coda: The move he singled out kept only a stone number, no name.

aws-s3-2017-typo.title: One Wide Argument
aws-s3-2017-typo.body: An S3 engineer ran an authorized command meant to take a small number of billing servers offline, but one input covered a wider range than intended. The removed servers also backed the index subsystem, which had not been fully restarted in years and came back far slower than expected.
aws-s3-2017-typo.coda: The outage ran roughly four hours; AWS's own status page depended on the same systems.

gitlab-2017-rm-rf.title: Five Backups, Zero
gitlab-2017-rm-rf.body: An engineer meant to clear a lagging replica but deleted the PostgreSQL data directory on the primary instead, stopping seconds too late; roughly 300GB was already gone. GitLab found that of five backup and replication methods it had running, none could actually restore the data.
gitlab-2017-rm-rf.coda: Recovery relied on a snapshot someone happened to take six hours earlier.

attention-title-beatles-2017.title: A Title Borrowed From the Beatles
attention-title-beatles-2017.body: Eight Google researchers published "Attention Is All You Need" in June 2017; the title nods to the Beatles song "All You Need Is Love." The paper's stated aim was a sequence model for machine translation that dropped recurrent networks in favor of attention alone.
attention-title-beatles-2017.coda: All eight authors have since left Google.

cloudflare-2019-regex.title: The Fuse That Was Removed
cloudflare-2019-regex.body: A new WAF rule with a catastrophically backtracking regex pushed CPU on Cloudflare's global network to near 100 percent within seconds of deployment. The rule itself was ordinary; what let it detonate was a CPU-usage safeguard on regex rules quietly deleted weeks earlier in a refactor.
cloudflare-2019-regex.coda: The outage lasted 27 minutes and ended when the WAF was disabled globally.

requests-kenneth-reitz.title: Handing Over the Keys
requests-kenneth-reitz.body: Requests logs over 30 million downloads a month and became the standard HTTP client for Python. Kenneth Reitz released it on February 14, 2011. In 2019, after health problems, he handed control of the project to the Python Software Foundation.
requests-kenneth-reitz.coda: He has not returned to lead the project since stepping down.

linux-y2038-kernel-fix.title: Eighteen Years Early
linux-y2038-kernel-fix.body: 32-bit Unix systems will overflow their time_t counter on 19 January 2038. Linux 5.6, released in 2020, was the first kernel able to keep a 32-bit system running past that date. Applications still need a rebuild against a 64-bit time_t to actually benefit.
linux-y2038-kernel-fix.coda: The kernel was patched years before most 32-bit userspace caught up.

log4shell-eight-years.title: Eight Years Unread
log4shell-eight-years.body: Log4j sits inside most enterprise Java software; Wiz and EY found 93 percent of cloud environments exposed to Log4Shell. The flaw existed in the code since 2013. It was reported November 24, 2021 and disclosed publicly on December 10, rated CVSS 10.
log4shell-eight-years.coda: A handful of volunteers wrote the fix that reached millions of servers.

core-js-denis-pushkarev.title: The Patch Nobody Replaced
core-js-denis-pushkarev.body: core-js ships inside WhatsApp, Netflix, Apple and PayPal, logging roughly 250 million downloads a month. Its author, Denis Pushkarev, was in a fatal 2019 car accident, served about ten months in prison starting January 2020, and kept maintaining the library throughout.
core-js-denis-pushkarev.coda: Monthly donations fell from about 2,500 dollars to 400.

tesla-westinghouse-royalty.title: The Royalty Tesla Waived
tesla-westinghouse-royalty.body: Westinghouse's contract paid Tesla $2.50 per horsepower in royalties. In early 1891, with the company close to failure, Tesla released it from the royalty clause.
tesla-westinghouse-royalty.coda: In 1897 Westinghouse bought his patents outright for $216,000.

salk-polio-patent.title: The Sun Has No Patent
salk-polio-patent.body: Edward Murrow asked who owned the polio vaccine patent. Salk answered there was none, could you patent the sun. Foundation lawyers had already examined the question and found the vaccine lacked patentable novelty because of prior art.
salk-polio-patent.coda: The unpatented vaccine was later valued at seven billion dollars.

cobol-two-hundred-billion-lines.title: Two Hundred Billion Lines
cobol-two-hundred-billion-lines.body: By 1997 Gartner estimated 200 billion lines of COBOL running eighty percent of business programs worldwide. In 2020, as COVID-era unemployment claims surged, several US state governments publicly appealed for COBOL programmers to keep their decades-old benefits systems running.
cobol-two-hundred-billion-lines.coda: Six years have passed since that appeal.

sabre-sage-to-booking.title: From Radar to Reservations
sabre-sage-to-booking.body: American Airlines and IBM signed their partnership in 1957, adapting the Air Force's Cold War SAGE air-defense architecture into a booking system. SABRE ran its first online test in 1960 and launched fully in 1964, becoming the world's first online transaction processing system.
sabre-sage-to-booking.coda: The parent company still operates, more than sixty years later.

kay-objects-messaging.title: Objects, Not the Point
kay-objects-messaging.body: By 1967 Alan Kay was using "object-oriented" for a design built on cells or network nodes talking only through messages. He later wrote he was sorry he ever coined the term "objects," because it draws attention to the lesser idea and buries the one he meant: messaging.
kay-objects-messaging.coda: The word he regretted outlived the idea he meant it to carry.

voyager-68-kilobits.title: Around the broken chip
voyager-68-kilobits.body: Voyager 1 launched in September 1977. Forty-seven years out, a memory chip in its flight data subsystem failed, three percent of it corrupted beyond repair. On 20 April 2024 engineers rearranged the code around the damaged area and the signal came back.
voyager-68-kilobits.coda: Its generators may supply enough power to return engineering data until 2036.

gif-lzw-unisys.title: The Free Format That Wasn't
gif-lzw-unisys.body: CompuServe shipped GIF in June 1987 using LZW compression without realizing Sperry Corporation already held the patent on it. In December 1994 Unisys, formed from Sperry's merger, announced it would collect licensing fees, prompting developers to build PNG as a replacement.
gif-lzw-unisys.coda: The patents ran out worldwide in 2004, and only then was GIF free.

zimmermann-pgp-release.title: PGP Given Away, Then Investigated
zimmermann-pgp-release.body: Phil Zimmermann released PGP with its source code on public FTP in 1991, the first widely available public-key encryption program. US Customs opened a criminal investigation for export-control violations. It ran three years and was dropped without indictment in early 1996.
zimmermann-pgp-release.coda: Three years under investigation, no charges filed, no royalties ever collected.

json-good-not-evil.title: For Good, Not Evil
json-good-not-evil.body: Douglas Crockford's 2002 license for the JSON libraries adds one clause: the software shall be used for Good, not Evil. JSON itself spread free and unpatented into nearly every API on the internet, but that single sentence made the license incompatible with standard open-source terms.
json-good-not-evil.coda: The format became universal; the joke clause it shipped with did not survive contact with corporate legal.

sogou-movie-line.title: Sogou's Line Was a Joke First
sogou-movie-line.body: The 2001 comedy Big Shot's Funeral has a wordplay line about search engines: "They search Sohu, we search Sogou, everyone searches their own way." Three years later, in 2004, Sohu's team took the joke and launched it as a real search engine, Sogou.
sogou-movie-line.coda: The punchline became the product name, unedited.

tbl-double-slash.title: The Extra Slashes
tbl-double-slash.body: Tim Berners-Lee put "//" in front of the domain name when he designed the URL. In October 2009 he admitted, given the colon already there, the two slashes were not needed at all — "it seemed like a good idea at the time," he said.
tbl-double-slash.coda: Every URL since has still typed both of them.

bilibili-mikufans.title: Bilibili's First Name Was Mikufans
bilibili-mikufans.body: The site launched in June 2009 as Mikufans, built for fans of the vocaloid Hatsune Miku. In January 2010 it was renamed Bilibili, after a nickname the protagonist of a light novel series gives Misaka Mikoto — an onomatopoeia for electric discharge.
bilibili-mikufans.coda: The renamed site kept the name through every subsequent redesign.

kuaishou-gif-app.title: Kuaishou Began as a GIF App
kuaishou-gif-app.body: Kuaishou launched in March 2011 as GIF Kuaishou, a phone app for making and sharing GIF images. In 2012 it pivoted to short video, and in 2014 the GIF prefix was dropped, leaving the name it carries as a video platform today.
kuaishou-gif-app.coda: The GIF prefix is gone; the underlying company name never changed.

zhihu-invite-only.title: Zhihu Needed an Invitation
zhihu-invite-only.body: Zhihu went live on January 26, 2011, and for its first two years registration required an invitation code. Open sign-up did not arrive until March 2013. The name itself is classical Chinese for "do you know" — a question, not a slogan.
zhihu-invite-only.coda: Registration has required no invitation since March 2013.

hp-garage-palo-alto.title: The Garage on Addison Avenue
hp-garage-palo-alto.body: In 1938 David Packard and his wife rented the ground-floor apartment of a 1905 house at 367 Addison Avenue in Palo Alto. He and Bill Hewlett put 538 dollars into the one-car garage behind it and built their first product, an audio oscillator.
hp-garage-palo-alto.coda: The property is now on the National Register of Historic Places and is not open to visitors.

apple-crist-drive-garage.title: When the bedroom ran out
apple-crist-drive-garage.body: In 1976 Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak assembled the first Apple boards at the house Jobs's parents owned in Los Altos, California.
apple-crist-drive-garage.coda: In his bedroom first. The garage only later, when there was no space left.

huawei-nanyou-flat.title: A Flat in Nanyou Xincun
huawei-nanyou-flat.body: In September 1987 Huawei was registered in a residential block in Nanyou Xincun, Shenzhen, with 21,000 yuan of capital, fourteen employees, and six shareholders splitting the equity evenly.
huawei-nanyou-flat.coda: The company moved its headquarters out in 1989; the flat's tenancy as HQ ended there.

wojcicki-garage-menlo-park.title: The Garage She Rented Out
wojcicki-garage-menlo-park.body: In September 1998 Page and Brin rented a garage in Menlo Park from Susan Wojcicki for $1,700 a month. Google was incorporated there.
wojcicki-garage-menlo-park.coda: She later became YouTube's chief executive.

tencent-seg-403.title: Building 2, Room 403
tencent-seg-403.body: In November 1998 Tencent registered at room 403, building two, of the Saige technology park in Huaqiangbei, Shenzhen. The building was full of startups like it, and the door was no different from any other.
tencent-seg-403.coda: The room is kept open only to Tencent employees now, under the name Tencent Origin.

unitree-left-dji.title: Out of DJI
unitree-left-dji.body: During his master's, Wang Xingxing built an all-electric quadruped robot on his own and called it XDog. After graduating he took a job at DJI, and left it soon after.
unitree-left-dji.coda: Unitree was registered in the Binjiang district of Hangzhou in August 2016.

unitree-one-yuan-option.title: One yuan a share
unitree-one-yuan-option.body: In September 2017 Unitree signed option agreements with seventeen employees at one yuan per share. Further grants followed, held through a single employee vehicle.
unitree-one-yuan-option.coda: Eight years later the company opened the book on its IPO.

unitree-g1-price.title: Ninety-nine thousand
unitree-g1-price.body: Humanoid robots had been priced as laboratory equipment. Unitree put the G1 on sale at 99,000 yuan, roughly the price of an entry-level car.
unitree-g1-price.coda: By 2025 humanoids were 51.78 percent of its revenue, on 5,500 units shipped.
